hints: Focus on what ester Z is built from, look at the alcohol backbone in the centre and the three acid fragments attached to it.
Notice that Z contains a glycerol skeleton with two ethanoate groups ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$-) and one propanoate group ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2$-).
Think about which starting pair already contains the propanoate part and just needs ethanoic acid to esterify the two remaining -OH groups.
walkthrough:
**Decode the structure of ester Z**

Look carefully at the centre of Z. It is a 3-carbon chain with an oxygen on each carbon, so it comes from glycerol, $\text{CH}_2(\text{OH})\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2(\text{OH})$.

Now look at the three acyl groups: two are $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$- from ethanoic acid, one is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C=O}$- from propanoic acid.

**Recall how esters form with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$**

Carboxylic acid plus alcohol gives ester plus water, catalysed by concentrated sulfuric acid:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{R'OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
A partial ester with free -OH groups can react further with a carboxylic acid to add more ester groups.

**Find the pair that can build Z**

We need a starting material that already has the glycerol backbone plus the one propanoate group, leaving two free -OH groups to be esterified by ethanoic acid.

That is exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ plus $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{Z} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Ethanol plus $\text{CH}(\text{CO}_2\text{H})_3$ would give a triethyl ester of a tricarboxylic acid. The backbone would be $\text{CH}(\text{CO}_2^-)_3$, not a glycerol $\text{CH}_2$-CH-$\text{CH}_2$ backbone with three separate ester oxygens, so Z cannot form.
options.B: Y here is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{OCOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which already has one ethanoate and one propanoate and one free middle -OH. Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, cannot acetylate that -OH because it is not a carboxylic acid and has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$- group to donate.
options.C: Y is the monopropanoate of glycerol with two free -OH groups. X is ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. With conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the two -OH groups are esterified by ethanoic acid to give the two ethanoate groups in Z, while the propanoate group is already present.
options.D: Glycerol plus only ethanoic acid can only make ethanoate esters, such as the triethanoate. It has no source of the propanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$- group seen at the top of Z, so this mixed ester cannot be produced.
